messages:
maria: Heads up — after flipping KV quant to INT8 in the nightly serving job I see a puzzling perf regression for low-batch decode (batch=1, seq_len=512). p50 went from ~48ms -> ~54ms and p95 spiked more. Memory dropped ~20% which is good, but the latency hit is unexpected. Anyone else seeing this?

tony: saw something similar in my local runs. looks like kernel selection flipped to attn_int8 path which has fewer fused ops, so extra memcpy+reorder cost shows up when batching is small.

akiko: can you paste the exact flag you toggled? is it global-int8-kv or per-layer? in our calibration we were doing per-tensor scales.
maria: I enabled --kv-quant=int8 --kv-scale-mode=per_layer on dedicated nodes. command: `redwood-serve --model m3-7b --kv-quant int8 --kv-scale per_layer --batching min_batch=1`
sre-rook: perf-bot shows a rise in memcpy % on GPU kernels after the change, from trace 2024-10-23_02. nvtx shows extra memcpy around the attn path. attaching quick trace summary: memcpy_time went from 2%->11% of kernel time at batch=1.

perf-bot: auto-report: regression_detected=true, metric=p50_latency, delta=+12.5%, context=decode(batch=1,seq=512), commit=ae3d...

tony: interesting — that matches kernel selection heuristics. For small batch sizes we choose a low-latency FP16 fused-attn kernel; the INT8 path currently chooses an int8_attn kernel optimized for throughput which sacrifices fusion. we need the kernel selector to favor fewer memcpy ops when batch=1.
akiko: also check calibration distribution. per_layer scales with int8 can produce some outlier heads, which we clamp — clamp logic currently does a CPU fallback for a few layers (we saw one layer falling back to fp16 to avoid overflow). that fallback costs a memcpy and kernel switch.
maria: i can repro locally. quick profiling snippet:
```
# single-run profile
batch=1 seq=512 tokens=1
attn_int8_kernel launch 0.42ms
fp16_attn_kernel launch 0.18ms
kv_unpack memcpy 0.95ms
kv_quant_scale kernel 0.22ms
overall decode step 54.1ms
```

sre-rook: that kv_unpack memcpy is the smell. Why are we unpacking aligned int8 -> int32 on host? should be staying on device. maybe the quant format we wrote uses host-side calibration table.
tony: root-cause hypothesis: our int8 KV encoding currently stores per-tensor scale in host memory and an unpack path does a small scatter gather to build per-head scales on device, but for small batch it launches many small kernels causing overhead. Possible fixes: 1) unify scale layout to device-global per-layer so unpack is a single launch; 2) add a fast path in kernel selector to pick fp16-attn if batch<4; 3) implement fp8 hybrid for KV for first K layers where sensitivity is highest.
akiko: also observed small accuracy drift: lm-eval average ppl +0.4 on long-context tasks with int8-kv per_layer. Not huge but correlated with increased clipping in generation. fp8-kv (e4m2) kept ppl within +0.05 but memory savings less than int8.
maria: can we try mixed approach: int8 for keys, fp8 for values? in decode the key access pattern is heavier for compute while values are summed into moments — not sure.
tony: technically possible: key ops use matmul->kv-cache index, values are read and combined; mixing precision will need consistent scaling in attention accumulators. Might reduce memcpy if we keep keys aligned to original layout.
sre-rook: experiment plan proposed: run matrix of {kv-format: [fp16,int8,fp8,mixed(k=int8,v=fp8)], batch=[1,2,4,8], seq=[128,512,2048]} and capture: p50/p95, GPU memcpy%, occupancy, model quality (ppl on held prompts). Let's prioritize batch=1/seq=512 because it's our worst.
akiko: calibration note: our per_layer scales were computed from a 2048-step calibration window with random prompts. For long-context models that has variance — perhaps use layerwise clipped-mad cal instead of global max to reduce outliers. Also try asymmetric quant (scale+zero_point) vs symmetric; asymmetric reduced overflow but adds an extra add op which is cheap compared to memcpy.
maria: I ran mixed(k=int8,v=fp8) quickly: mem drop ~18%, p50 ~49ms (so better than int8 both latency and mem compromise), quality delta ~+0.08 ppl. Will push more runs.
tony: actionable items: 1) update kernel selector heuristic to prefer fused fp16-attn path when batch<=2 unless explicit throughput flag set. 2) remove host-side per-head scale scatter by storing scale table in device-global contiguous array (low-risk). 3) run calibration variants (max, mad, percentile-clamp) and measure quality vs overflow count.
sre-rook: i'll file a tracking issue and schedule a short perf-window with infra to run the matrix overnight.
maria: thanks — i'll attach logs from my run in the thread and share nvprof samples. if we can get a patch to kernel selector and a device-scale table quick, we can try a canary next week. :thumbsup:
